summary: I checked whether this is genuinely simpler or whether complexity moved: I diffed every runtime module against 26b5203, inventoried every numeric constant and every declared name for reachability, counted hot-path calls by role on both corpora, and probed the horizon logic with the repo's own offline scripted transport. The universality properties hold cleanly - one orchestrator, one entry point, no scenario-specific branch, no question-keyword routing, no probabilities/weights/scores/particles/branches, no capability menu or fixed action vocabulary, no random or numeric library imports. But the simplification is much smaller than claimed (net -168 of 3,362 lines; trajectory.py churned 428 lines to shed 20; the only real deletion is world_mind.py's 176-line event-review block) and two of the replacement mechanisms are not wired. reached_horizon can never be set, because every schedule site refuses anything past the cutoff, so NO_AT_CUTOFF is reachable only if an event lands on the cutoff instant exactly - I demonstrated this, and the one test guarding it passes only because the fixture's window is exactly 7x2 days. And the power to delete a valid world answer was not taken away, it was moved into code and made unconditional: it fired on 12.6% of world calls in the frozen corpus, on substantive acts as well as non-events, on answers the world prompt itself holds out as correct, and it is recorded in neither code_overrides.jsonl nor trajectory.md. Eight further declared-but-unwired names remain - the exact defect class the branch says it eliminated.

findings.title: reached_horizon is unreachable dead state: nothing can ever be scheduled past the cutoff, so the honest NO is structurally impossible and the report's diagnosis of its own gap is wrong
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:196 (declared), :871 (`reached_horizon['yes'] = ev is not None`, requires ev.t > cutoff), :1018-1029 (the only reader). Every schedule site refuses t > cutoff: trajectory.py:215 (`if due > cutoff or due <= world.clock.now: return False`), trajectory.py:384 (`if due <= cutoff:` else only a trace note at :398), adapter.py:98 (`elif when <= cutoff:`). world.schedule() is called nowhere else on the semantic path (world.py:177 is send_info, world.py:250 is run_ops; World.apply cannot schedule). Probe with the repo's own offline transport, world returning `after: 25 days` on a 14-day window: 1 event_beyond_cutoff note, 0 ledger records scheduled past the cutoff, status incomplete_empty_queue, answer UNRESOLVED. Corpus: artifacts/final_v6/cold_email lived 332.0h of its 336.0h window (98.8%) and holiday_deposit 74.8h of 75.3h (99.2%), both incomplete_empty_queue. Corpus cutoffs are 07:00, 09:00, 17:00, 18:00, 20:00, 23:59:59 - instants no world-authored duration will hit.
findings.why_it_matters: traj.status == 'cutoff', the only status under which NO_AT_CUTOFF may be returned, requires world.clock.now >= cutoff, which requires the queue to land on the cutoff instant to the second. The alternative signal - the world saying the next thing lies beyond the deadline - is computed at trajectory.py:384, written to a trace note, and thrown away before reached_horizon could see it. So 'the horizon honestly reached' is not a case the code can enter, one of three STATUSES members is effectively unreachable, and the corpus's 0 NO_AT_CUTOFF is a structural consequence, not the honest cost the report presents. SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FINAL_COMPLETION_REPORT.md:207-212 attributes the gap to a missing wake provenance (known_deadline); my probe shows a run whose future is fully known and entirely beyond the deadline still returns incomplete_empty_queue, so no wake provenance fixes it. The runtime is not failing to reach its deadlines - it reaches 92-99% of the window and then cannot cross the last inch.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat 'the queue is empty and the world's proposed futures all fell beyond the cutoff' as reaching the horizon - set reached_horizon when an event_beyond_cutoff is noted, or drop reached_horizon and decide the horizon from whether the last sweep produced any schedulable future - and add a test whose window is not an exact multiple of the wake interval.

findings.title: The power to delete a valid world answer was moved into code, not removed: the attention rule deleted 12.6% of all world answers in the frozen corpus, including substantive acts, and the world prompt explicitly authorises what it deletes
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:332-339 deletes any event returned for a pending_progression trigger unless `envelope['observed'] and actor_id in envelope['for']`. The same prompt invites exactly those answers: world_mind.py:39 gives "he does not look at his phone all afternoon" as a canonical correct answer, and world_mind.py:147-151 says the item "may simply sit there untouched while that person deals with other things. Any of those is a legitimate answer; say which one actually happens." Corpus: 58 deletions across 8 of 11 runs (artifacts/final_v6/*/structural_refusals.jsonl) against 459 world calls = 12.6%; per run 21 holiday_deposit, 15 group_coordination, 7 cold_email, 6 anti_stereotype, 6 feedback_deadline. Not only non-events: anti_stereotype c18 "Ethel's call is answered by the vendor support representative"; anti_stereotype c30 "The vendor support representative acknowledges Ethel's reference number and says they will look up the account and guide her through the pairing steps"; holiday_deposit c150 "Ruth calls Marian Prowse to explain that Dev has pulled out and Nina is still undecided, and asks if the deposit deadline can be extended by a day"; evidence_responsive c12 "Marcus Bell replies to Dana Whitfield that the hall is confirmed for the 14th". cold_email spent 7 of its 56 world calls this way and committed 2 events.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the shape the branch exists to remove - two rules that cannot both be satisfied, and the answer destroyed - with code in the LLM's place. It is worse in three ways than the reviewer it replaced: there is no correction attempt, there is no possibility of the rule being satisfied when the honest answer is 'attention did not arrive', and unlike the event reviewer it cannot be overridden. Because did_it is None for pending_progression triggers, the identity re-routing at trajectory.py:346 never applies here, so a world answer naming someone else as the chooser is deleted rather than handed to them - the mechanism the report presents as the fix ("control routes to that person") fired 0 times in 459 world calls. Every deleted call is also a paid call that advances nothing, and each deletion removes the only thing that could have scheduled a consequence, which is one of the ways the queue empties.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop asking the question whose only permitted answer is yes: either accept 'their notice did not reach it' as a valid, event-free answer (judgment plus wake, no event) instead of deleting the response, or narrow the refusal to events that restate an item's existing state and route a named chooser to that person as their turn.

findings.title: Near-identical duplicate suppression does not exist; the completion test that certifies it passes because the run makes exactly one world call
findings.evidence: tests/test_runtime_completion.py:154-179 (`test_the_same_physical_act_is_not_committed_twice`), docstring: "Near-identical, not byte-identical: the merged guard was an exact casefold match, and a woman signed one lease twice a minute apart." The only duplicate rule in the runtime is still an exact casefold match: world_mind.py:236 `if env is not None and contained(env['description']).casefold() in already_committed`. Re-running that test's own transport and instrumenting it: 1 world call, 1 step, status incomplete_empty_queue, 1 signing committed - the second string is never generated, so the assertion `len(signings) <= 1` is satisfied without any dedup. Corpus proof the behaviour is unfixed, artifacts/final_v6/holiday_deposit: e789 "Ruth calls Marian Prowse and says the deposit won't be coming, so they will have to release Cove Cottage" (12:00:00) and e819 "Ruth calls Marian Prowse and tells her the deposit won't be coming, so they will have to release Cove Cottage" (12:01:00); e804 and e863, the same "Marian Prowse answers the phone and hears Ruth say the deposit won't be coming" a minute apart; e873 and e884, the same text to Nina; e891/e902/e916/e939, Marian dialling the Leeds couple four times.
findings.why_it_matters: A test written to fail on merged main and pass here is being counted as evidence that a defect is fixed, and the defect is not fixed - the mechanism it names was never written. SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:76 already classified the exact-casefold rule REDUNDANT ("near-identical duplicates commit freely") and nothing acted on it. holiday_deposit's 91 committed events are inflated by this, which is also why it exhausts its window: the same act recommitted is a step spent and a call spent.
findings.suggested_fix: Either implement the near-identical check the test's docstring describes and keep the test, or delete the test and record the exact-casefold rule as a known-partial guard rather than a completed fix.

findings.title: follow_up is still instructed in the live world prompt, contradicts the delivery rule in the same prompt, and is consumed by nothing
findings.evidence: world_mind.py:129-130 keeps `"follow_up": true` in the response template; world_mind.py:154-160 spends seven lines defining it, ending "When it is false, nothing further is asked and the next thing to happen is somebody's decision or a later scheduled event"; envelope.py:7,13-19,152,165-167,199 validate and preserve it; world_mind.py:249 carries it into event_checked. No reader: `grep -rn follow_up sworldmodel/` shows trajectory.py:664 only, and that is a comment ("THE TRANSPORT CHAIN IS GONE"). The instruction also contradicts world_mind.py:37 in the same prompt: :37 forbids writing that anything "arrives, lands in an inbox, is delivered... is still unread, is still waiting", while :154-156 tells the world follow_up is true when "something is in transit, something is underway, something will arrive".
findings.why_it_matters: The report and the audit both list the follow_up chain as deleted; only the consumer was deleted. The producer instruction is intact, so the world is still being told, in the hot path, that a field it writes controls whether it will be asked again - which is false - and is still being primed to think in transit stages by the same prompt that forbids narrating them. That is a declared-but-unwired vocabulary in the one place it costs most: inside a live prompt, biasing every world answer. It is also two mutually unsatisfiable instructions in one prompt, which is the precise failure the audit says organises everything else.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete follow_up from WORLD_SYSTEM, from validate_event's accepted fields, and from event_checked.

findings.title: Eight declared-but-unwired names remain in the runtime, the defect class the branch claims to have eliminated
findings.evidence: MAX_ENV_CHAIN = 1 at trajectory.py:557 is never read (its only comparison site was deleted with the follow_up chain), and env_chain at :558 is only ever assigned 0 at :585, :610, :679. OP_TURN_ABANDONED is imported at trajectory.py:32 and declared at journal.py:32 with no writer. abandoned_turns at trajectory.py:102 is never incremented but is exported by to_dict() at :111 and appears as `"abandoned_turns": 0` in all 11 artifacts/final_v6/*/runtime_metrics.json. Status incomplete_review_failure is documented at trajectory.py:85 and never set. world_step's `intention` parameter (trajectory.py:237) is passed at :524 and unreferenced in the function body. attempt_id is written (trajectory.py:517-525, journal.py:61,133) and read by nothing in the runtime - only tests/test_runtime_completion.py:292-296 - and the world is never shown it, contrary to SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:141-143 ("the world is given that id and must cite it"). Trace kinds event_abandoned and actor_turn_abandoned are still collected at trace.py:94-96 and rendered at trace.py:168-179 with nothing emitting them. choice_returned_to_its_owner (trajectory.py:351, trace.py:85) fired 0 times in 459 world calls.
findings.why_it_matters: SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:153-156 states that a declared-but-unwired vocabulary has been the direct cause of three separate live defects in this codebase, and the report's before/after table counts 3 wake provenances and 2 exception classes removed. Five dead names were removed and at least eight were retained or newly created - one of them (reached_horizon) is the subject of my first CRITICAL, so the pattern has already caused a fourth live defect on this branch. attempt_id in particular is presented as the enforcement of "every world consequence cites an attempt", but code stamps the id by construction, so it can never be wrong and can never detect the failure it was introduced for. SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FINAL_COMPLETION_REPORT.md:106-108 lists semantic.actor_turn_abandoned as a code-owned state transition that exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete MAX_ENV_CHAIN, env_chain, the OP_TURN_ABANDONED import and declaration, abandoned_turns, the incomplete_review_failure line, world_step's intention parameter, and the two dead trace kinds; then either give the world the attempt_id and check that it cites it, or drop attempt_id.

findings.title: The only code overrule that actually happens is absent from code_overrides.jsonl and from trajectory.md, which is the exact artifact defect trace.py's own comment claims to have fixed
findings.evidence: trace.py:86-91: "Every place code overruled the model... A run whose decisive act was proposed and refused twice looked, in the artifacts, exactly like a run in which the world judged that nothing happened." The code_overrides list at trace.py:93-97 contains event_abandoned, duplicate_event_dropped, duration_floored, actor_turn_abandoned, group_observation_split, progression_skipped - not attention_answer_without_attention, the 58-occurrence category. render_trajectory has a branch for event_abandoned (trace.py:168-179, now unemittable) and none for attention_answer_without_attention. Consequence in artifacts/final_v6/cold_email/trajectory.md: all 7 deleted world answers render as "- proposes: (no concrete event yet)", identical to a genuine "nothing happened" judgment; `grep -c "does not look at his phone" cold_email/trajectory.md` returns 0. The 12 dead lines of event_abandoned rendering are kept alive by tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:775-800, which injects the trace kind by hand and asserts "Proposed and refused twice" appears in trajectory.md.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of the artifacts cannot distinguish "the world judged that nothing happened" from "the world said something happened and code deleted it" - the precise confusion trace.py says it eliminated. Because a test injects the obsolete kind, the trace layer looks covered while the live overrule is invisible, and the aggregate code_overrides count (36 across the corpus) understates what code did by a factor of 2.6.
findings.suggested_fix: Add attention_answer_without_attention to the code_overrides list and give it a render branch; delete the event_abandoned branch and the test that keeps it alive.

findings.title: MAX_EVENTS_PER_INSTANT measures crowding at the wrong instant, so the cap it advertises is trivially bypassed
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:275-280 counts committed and pending events at `here = _iso_now(world)`, i.e. the CURRENT clock instant, but the event is scheduled at `world.clock.now + delta` (trajectory.py:383). The floor at :377-382 only applies when delta is zero, so any non-zero duration lands unchecked on a destination instant that may already be full. Corpus: artifacts/final_v6/holiday_deposit has 5 committed events on 2026-09-15T12:02:00 (e873, e881, e884, e891, e902) against a cap of 3, plus 3 each on 12:00:00 and 12:01:00, while duration_floored fired 19 times across the corpus. The seven-line comment at trajectory.py:38-44 says "A hundred events on a single timestamp is not a sequence of events"; SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:77 already classified this constant REDUNDANT and it was carried over unchanged.
findings.why_it_matters: The number 3 and the 1-minute floor are code's own inventions deciding how fast life moves, and they do not deliver the property their comment claims. Either the check should count the destination instant (in which case the constant is load-bearing and should be justified) or it is decoration and should go, per the branch's own default that nothing is kept merely because it exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Count events already committed or pending at `world.clock.now + delta` rather than at `world.clock.now`, or delete the constant and its floor.

findings.title: budget_for's derivation and docstring are stale: they price a per-event read-only review that no longer exists
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:60-73. The docstring states "An actor turn and a world event each carry a read-only review, and a rejected one is asked again, so a turn costs up to four calls rather than one and an adjudication up to four rather than two" - the world event review was removed on this branch. The formula still doubles the world side: `per_turn = 2 * (2 + 2 * MAX_INTENTIONS_PER_TURN)` = 16 where the real cost is `2 * (2 + 1 * 3)` = 10, and `per_step`'s leading 2 is world-plus-review where only the world call remains. With run_simulation.py's default --max-steps 250 and 4 actors this yields a ceiling above 34,000 calls; the largest corpus run spent 638.
findings.why_it_matters: The function's entire justification is that it is "derived from the runtime's own structural caps rather than picked" (trajectory.py:54-56). A formula derived from a removed mechanism is a picked number wearing a derivation, and the docstring asserts a component of the runtime that is gone - a comment describing a mechanism that does not exist, in the one place where the honesty of the cutoff status depends on the number being right.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-derive per_turn and per_step from the four surviving roles and rewrite the docstring to name only them.

findings.title: The headline reduction claims overstate: 6->4 gates is really 5->4, and the removed reviewer was 11.9% of hot-path calls, not "roughly half"
findings.evidence: SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FINAL_COMPLETION_REPORT.md:99-101 ("Per step the hot path passes through 4 semantic gates where it passed through 6") and SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:161 ("removes two of six live LLM roles and roughly half the calls on the hot path"). Measured per-step gates: main = world, event_review, actor, continuity, judge (5); branch = world, actor, continuity, judge (4). The verifier is not per-step (trajectory.py:723, called only on a candidate answer) and is counted on the before side only. Measured call composition: artifacts/baseline_main (5 runs) world 398, event_review 137, actor 266, continuity 266, judge 84, verifier 4 = 1,155, so event_review was 11.9%; artifacts/final_v6 (11 runs) world 459, actor 421, continuity 419, judge 237, verifier 14 = 1,550. Only one of the two reviewers was removed: actor_mind.py is byte-identical to 26b5203.
findings.why_it_matters: The claim that half the hot path was removed is the main quantitative support for "this is simpler". The actual reduction is one gate of five and roughly an eighth of the calls, against a line-count change of -168 of 3,362 (-5.0%) in which trajectory.py churned 428 lines to shed 20 and the only substantive deletion is world_mind.py's 176-line event-review block. Complexity mostly moved: two mechanisms left (the event-review loop, the follow_up chain) and four arrived (reached_horizon, attempt_id, the by-identity check, the attention refusal), two of which are unwired.
findings.suggested_fix: State the measured figures - 5 per-step gates to 4, event_review 11.9% of baseline calls, runtime -5.0% lines - and drop the 6->4 and half-the-calls claims.

findings.title: MAX_WORLD_RUN can permanently swallow an owed arrival question, and neither it nor _hand_back_the_turn leaves any record
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:648-660: `arrivals_asked[(aid, rec['event_id'])] = True` is set at :651 BEFORE the `if since_actor['n'] >= MAX_WORLD_RUN: break` at :652-653. The pair is then permanently marked as asked (the `continue` at :649-650 skips it forever) although the world was never asked. Reachable whenever an event has two or more unseen recipients and the first world_step at :654 pushes since_actor to 6 (MAX_WORLD_RUN, trajectory.py:567) - group_coordination and holiday_deposit both have four actors. _hand_back_the_turn (trajectory.py:573-591) emits no note() at all, and neither does the :652 break, so neither appears in code_overrides.jsonl, structural_refusals.jsonl or trajectory.md.
findings.why_it_matters: MAX_WORLD_RUN = 6 is an arbitrary number of code's own invention deciding whose turn it is - the runtime's most directly social constant - and it can silently and permanently cancel a question the runtime decided was owed. An arrival never asked about produces no consequence and no wake, which is one of the ways the queue empties, and there is no artifact in which a reader could find that it happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the arrivals_asked marking after the successful world_step, and note() both the hand-back and the deferral so they appear in code_overrides.jsonl.

findings.title: The continuity reviewer was not narrowed as the audit prescribed; it is 27% of all hot-path calls and changes 4.8% of turns
findings.evidence: actor_mind.py is byte-identical to 26b5203 (`git diff 26b5203 HEAD -- sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/actor_mind.py` is empty), so CONTINUITY_SYSTEM still carries the realism criteria the audit said must move offline: actor_mind.py:266-269 "reads as a generic person going through the motions", "plays up a stereotype their evidence does not support", "goes over an unchanged question again merely because time has passed", plus :257-258 "abandons or reverses a plan they still hold". SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:59 and :118-122 prescribe "narrow to exactly" a direct factual contradiction with the actor's own authorised record. Measured: 419 continuity calls of 1,550 total (27.0%); artifacts/final_v6/*/actor_continuity_reviews.jsonl gives 394 PASS and 25 REVISE, and the ledgers give 5 OVERRULED, so 20 of 421 turns (4.8%) were changed.
findings.why_it_matters: Only the reviewer's ability to destroy a turn was removed; its scope was not touched. It is now the second-largest consumer of the call budget, still holds opinions about realism and stereotype that the audit classified as belonging offline, and buys a 4.8% intervention rate whose value is not measured anywhere. Against the branch's own default - where a model must judge, it must not judge what structure can, and nothing is kept merely because it exists - this is the largest remaining unexamined cost on the hot path.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut CONTINUITY_SYSTEM to the factual-contradiction clauses the audit named, and report the corpus intervention rate so the remaining cost is justified by measurement.

findings.title: 52% -> 14% machinery is not a matched comparison: of the four scenarios present in both corpora, one regressed and one is unchanged
findings.evidence: `python3 evaluation/interface_mechanics.py` reproduces both aggregates (baseline_main 40/77 = 52%, final_v6 30/209 = 14%) and evaluation/interface_mechanics.py is byte-identical to 26b5203, so the metric definition is sound. Per run on the four scenarios in both: cold_email 2/3 (67%) -> 1/2 (50%); group_coordination 28/56 (50%) -> 2/26 (8%); lease_return 3/8 (38%) -> 6/10 (60%); plumber_confirm 1/2 (50%) -> 1/2 (50%). The aggregate drop is carried by three long runs that have no baseline counterpart (holiday_deposit 11/91, feedback_deadline 3/31, anti_stereotype 3/26), and the baseline corpus has 77 events against the branch's 209.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the headline evidence that the transport chain actually left rather than moved, and the implementer has already had to withdraw one matched-pair inference the sample size could not support. On the matched subset the picture is one large improvement, one regression, one unchanged and one marginal - and holiday_deposit still commits "the call rings through to their phone", "Marian Prowse dials the number of the couple from Leeds" and "Ruth's call rings through to Marian Prowse's phone" (e939, e891, and 14:05), so the vocabulary shifted from inboxes to telephony rather than disappearing.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the four matched scenarios alongside the aggregate, and name the regression in lease_return rather than letting the corpus-wide average stand alone.

findings.title: The frozen corpus under review is gitignored while 1,203 superseded artifact files stay tracked, including the full baseline it is compared against
findings.evidence: .gitignore ends with `artifacts/final_v*/*/`, so artifacts/final_v6 contributes exactly 3 tracked files (FROZEN_SHA.txt, RUNTIME_FREEZE.txt, SUMMARY.txt) while all eleven run directories are untracked (`git status --ignored` lists them). artifacts/baseline_main is fully tracked at 111 files despite the matching `artifacts/baseline_main/*/` rule, because it was committed before the rule. Tracked artifact files at HEAD: 1,203 - matched_pairs 440, semantic_runtime_v1_baseline 241, simulations 226, baseline_main 111, scene_targeted 51.
findings.why_it_matters: The rule "generated runs are evidence, not source" was applied to the evidence that supports this branch and not to the evidence it supersedes, which is the wrong way round for review: on a fresh clone every measurement in the report - 209 events, 14% machinery, 58 structural refusals, 11/11 replay exact - is unverifiable, while 1,203 files of older corpora that nobody needs remain in the diff. The 4,079 -> 1,203 reduction is real, but the audit's BLOAT verdict (SINGLE_TRAJECTORY_FIRST_PRINCIPLES_AUDIT.md:81) applies equally to what was kept.
findings.suggested_fix: Either track the frozen corpus under review or make it regenerable from a committed manifest, and apply the same rule to matched_pairs, semantic_runtime_v1_baseline, simulations and baseline_main.

findings.title: Stale test scaffolding for the removed event_review role, including one now-vacuous test
findings.evidence: tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:94 (role_of still returns "event_review"), :67, :112, :246, :1766, :1859 return PASSES for a role nothing asks. tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:1946 `test_a_persons_own_intention_is_already_their_choice` scripts an event_review returning ACTOR_TURN_REQUIRED and asserts the reply survives - the branch is never taken, so the test now asserts only that a scripted world event gets committed, which holds regardless. tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:775-800 injects the event_abandoned trace kind by hand.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead scaffolding makes the suite look like it still covers a gate that is gone, and one test in the 85 that pass has lost its subject entirely - so the pass count overstates coverage of the new design.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the event_review arm from role_of, Script and reviewed, and delete or rewrite the two tests whose subject no longer exists.

findings.title: The transport samples at temperature 0.7 while the runtime's own prompts and docstrings forbid sampling
findings.evidence: llm.py:107 `payload = {"model": self.model, "temperature": 0.7, ...}` (unchanged from 26b5203), against world_mind.py:100 "Never sample or randomise" and trajectory.py:2-4 "No branching, no sampling, no probabilities, no particles". The runtime imports no random, numpy, scipy or statistics module and contains no probability, weight, score, particle or branch construct - the only hit for those words is views.py:6 disclaiming them - so the sampling is entirely in the provider parameter.
findings.why_it_matters: "One concrete trajectory" is one draw from a distribution at temperature 0.7, so the corpus is reproducible only through the ledger, never from the same inputs. That is defensible, but the modules assert the stronger property, and an arbitrary numeric constant chosen nowhere in the design is the thing deciding how much the world varies.
findings.suggested_fix: State that the trajectory is one sampled draw and that reproducibility comes from the ledger, and justify or lower 0.7 explicitly.

findings.title: A superseded compiler with a capability graph is retained as a flag-gated alternate path
findings.evidence: compiler/legacy/ holds 15 modules including capabilities.py, causal_discovery.py, graph_builder.py and world_graph.py, reachable via compile_question.py:66-67 under `--compiler legacy` (compiler/__init__.py:10-11). adapter.py:14-16 states "There is no capability graph, action ontology, causal program, second WorldSpec, handler registry or effect language between the manifest and the runtime" - true of the semantic runtime's path, and run_simulation.py uses compiler.compile_scene only. `git diff 26b5203 HEAD -- compiler/` is empty, so this branch did not touch it. The semantic runtime itself has exactly one orchestrator and one production entry point, with tests/test_runtime_completion.py:493 asserting a single `def run_trajectory`.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a second, differently-shaped compilation path containing precisely the constructs the design rules out, kept because it exists. It is frozen and flag-gated, so it does not affect the runtime under review - but the branch's stated default ("nothing is kept merely because it exists") has not been applied to it.
findings.suggested_fix: Record compiler/legacy explicitly as frozen dead weight with a removal decision, rather than leaving it as an undiscussed alternate path.
